query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn system was selected to reduce cost while retaining the mechanical performance of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi; prior work reported comparable or better mechanical properties after excluding Co. Research on FeNiCrMn has mainly addressed corrosion, while studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys examined dynamic responses under tension or compression, different temperatures and strain rates, compositional changes, and the presence of cracks or voids. Those studies established that dynamic properties are sensitive to loading regime and material condition, but their different chemistries and defect states do not identify what governs FeNiCrMn. Under the constraints of retaining the Co-free composition and its strength–ductility balance, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains the dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes? Define a controlled study capable of testing the hypothesis, its applicable boundaries, the prior findings that support it, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Under dynamic loading, the Co‐free FeNiCrMn alloy’s increased yield strength and strain-rate sensitivity result from a strain-rate and temperature dependent dislocation mechanism. Specifically, at high strain rates and lower temperatures, limited dynamic recovery causes rapid dislocation accumulation and the nucleation of adiabatic shear bands, which in turn enhance strain hardening and help maintain a strength–ductility balance.
generation.material_initial_state: As-solidified, cast Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy with its established microstructure (e.g. a predominantly FCC or related solid solution structure typical of solidified medium‐entropy alloys) that yields a balanced strength–ductility in quasi‐static tests.
generation.intervention: Conduct a controlled mechanical testing study where identical samples are deformed under compression across a range of strain rates—from quasi‐static (10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ to 100 s⁻¹) to high strain rates (using a split-Hopkinson pressure bar at ≈1300–2100 s⁻¹)—and at different temperatures (room temperature and elevated conditions), while keeping the processing and material composition unchanged.
generation.conditions: Samples prepared via a consistent casting route will be tested under ambient conditions for quasi-static loading and in a split-Hopkinson setup for dynamic loading; temperature will be controlled via an environmental chamber or pre-heating, with strain rate and temperature being the main controlled variables.
generation.structural_mediator: The evolution of dislocation density and the formation of adiabatic shear bands within the microstructure.
generation.mechanism: At lower strain rates, dislocation motion produces steady strain hardening. However, at high strain rates, especially at lower temperatures, insufficient time for dynamic recovery leads to rapid dislocation accumulation, which then nucleates localized adiabatic shear bands that significantly enhance yield strength. At higher temperatures, thermally activated dislocation mobility promotes recovery, reducing the yield strength despite high strain rates.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to quasi-static conditions, dynamic tests at lower temperatures will show an increase in yield strength due to pronounced dislocation accumulation and shear band formation, while tests at elevated temperatures will show a reduced yield strength increase because of enhanced dislocation mobility and dynamic recovery.
generation.baseline: Mechanical properties (yield strength and strain hardening rate) measured under quasi-static conditions at ambient temperature for the as-solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies to the as-solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy with its inherent microstructure and established strength–ductility balance; deviations in processing that alter the microstructure significantly or tests conducted far beyond moderate temperature ranges might not follow this behavior.
generation.uncertainty: The exact quantitative contribution of dislocation accumulation versus potential contributions from twinning or other deformation modes remains unclear, and the precise strain-rate thresholds for shear band formation need to be established.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a set of Co-free FeNiCrMn samples using identical casting methods. Subject these samples to compression tests at a range of strain rates (quasi-static to high dynamic using a split-Hopkinson pressure bar) and at various controlled temperatures (ambient and elevated). Employ in situ high-speed imaging (where available) and post-deformation microstructural analysis (via EBSD/TEM) to quantify dislocation densities and detect the presence of adiabatic shear bands.
measurements: Dynamic yield strength and flow stress curves
Dislocation density and distribution from EBSD/TEM
Occurrence, size, and morphology of adiabatic shear bands
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the dynamic yield strength and strain hardening behavior do not correlate with a significant increase in dislocation density and the appearance of shear bands (or if another mechanism such as twinning is observed to dominate without the predicted effects), then the mechanistic hypothesis is falsified.

The equiatomic NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy prepared by arc melting has a single crystallographic structure. Mechanical properties and microstructure of the NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy deformed at high strain rates (900 s−1 to 4600 s−1) were investigated. The yield strength of the NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy is sensitive to the change of high strain rates. Serration behaviors were also observed on the flow stress curves of the alloy deformed at the strain rates ranging from 900 s−1 to 4600 s−1. The Zerilli–Armstrong constitutive equation can be used to predict the flow stress curves of the NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy. Large amounts of deformation bands led to obvious serration behaviors of the NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy under dynamic loading.
